decision: Imports validate and publish row by row; bad rows wait instead of failing the file
why: A 1,800-row seller feed with 14 bad rows should publish 1,786 products now, not zero.
value: Sellers go live sooner and errors are small, specific fixes.

decision: Job progress is computed from the job's start and rate, so every tab shows the same number
why: Polling per tab would drift and cost requests; a deterministic projection stays consistent.
alternative: Poll a progress endpoint every second.
value: Consistent progress across tabs with no extra traffic.

decision: Errors open in a drawer as a table of row, field, value, problem and a suggested fix
why: Merchandisers fix data, not stack traces; showing the value next to the fix makes each decision a click.
value: Feeds get fixed in minutes, inside the tool.

decision: Accepted fixes become seller mappings the agent reuses on the next feed
why: Sellers repeat their quirks ('SND' for sand, 'GG' for XL); remembering them turns a recurring error into a one-time fix.
value: Error rates fall with every import.

decision: Seller columns stay in their terse legacy form in the feed and are mapped at the edge
why: An anti-corruption layer keeps sellers' formats out of Maré's catalog model.
alternative: Ask every seller to adopt Maré's schema.
value: Onboarding a seller takes days, not a data migration.
